Adoption Criteria .a Here are the minimum requirements we need to see in your setup before we can approve an adoption. • An Enclosure at least IOOx50cm, all on one level with a secure lid and a lot of ventilation. • A 28cm+ upright wheel for Syrian and Chinese hamsters and 21cm+ for Russian and Robo hamsters. • A minimum of 20cm+ safe bedding across the entire setup. • A sand bath with hamster safe sand and no smaller than 25cm+. • 3 different substrates e.g beech chips, coco soil and cork granule. • Platforms to place heavy items on. • 3 hides/tunnels, openings should be no smaller than 7cm for Syrian hamsters. • A variety of sprays e.g Sorghum, Flax or Millet. • Species specific seed mix, we're happy to give suggestions. • Water bowl/bottle, 2 sources is recommended. A safe branch e.g Java wood or Bamboo root is not essential but it is ideal. BRIGHT HORIZON HAMSTER RESCUE Registered Charity Number 1210796 Brighthorizonhamster.co.uk

text: Feeding guide Syrian: IS-2 teaspoons per day/ Itablespoon every other day Dwarf: flat teaspoon every day Robo: 1-1.5 teaspoons every other day Food intake depends on the hamster. Some hamsters may be bigger or smaller for their species so this needs to be taken into consideration. More active hamsters may need more food. Age can also play a role into how much food they need. All hamsters can have 3/4 lots of fresh food every week. Dwarfs can only have 1 piece of fruit every 2 weeks as they are prone to diabetes however all other species can have around 2 pieces per week. The easiest way to know if you are feeding the correct amount of food is weighing them (in grams) weekly and keeping track of their weight to make sure it doesn't increase or decrease too much (if it fluctuates greatly this may be a sign of illness so you need to take them to an exotic vet asap). BRIGHT HORIZON HAMSTER RESCUE

Unfortunately, many places still sell unsafe wheels and buyers are unaware of their dangers. NUMBER

text: In the wild, hamsters dig into the ground to create a series of intricate, connected holes and tunnels to live in. These are used to store food and shelter from predators and environmental changes. TUh'Mf1 But why do domestic hamsters need to do this? A hamster's natural burrow system. text: My hamster just grooms herself, I don't think she uses the sand bath Hamsters are very cleanly animals and regularly groom themselves, however self-grooming isn't enough to keep them clean. Hamsters produce natural oils to keep their fur healthy; sand is used to exfoliate and absorb any excess oil and dirt. Without access to a sand bath, it is common for hamsters to look "oily" due to a build up of this excess oil. Even if you don't see your hamster using the sand bath often, it is essential they have one to stay healthy. Plus, it's a great natural substrate for them to explore! NUMBER

text: Adoption Check List Multi- Chambers What is a multi-chamber hide? A multi-chamber is a large hide that mimics natural burrows with multiple sections. Hamsters will use the different areas to sleep, store food or go to the toilet. It's best to have one large multi- chamber hide in your enclosure. This should be made up of at least 3 sections. You can also include smaller versions with less chambers as additional hiding places.

text: But they are very small annals, why do they need so much space? My hamster was Fine in a small cage when I was younger. We understand that the minimum standards for hamster care have changed dramatically, particularly over the last ten years. However, these standards exist and develop purely for hamster welfare. They set the minimum requirements for humane, ethical care. Research and studies have established that hamsters require an enclosure size of 100x50x50cm. This space not only allows for adequate sized wheels and enrichment, but also enables hamsters to exhibit natural behaviours, including burrowing and foraging. Small cages result in severe stress behaviour, such as bar climbing and biting, which can cause serious injury. Therefore, 100x50x50cm is the minimum size recommendation by major organisations like Blue Cross, PDSA and Woodgreen. NUMBER

So it is essential to provide your hamster with a large dish full of hamster- safe sand for them to use. We recommend your hamster's sand bath should be around the size of an A4 piece of paper and at least 5cm deep. As they are native to the desert, Roborovski hamsters require a larger sand bath - 1/3 of the enclosure if possible! NUMBER

text: UNSAFE I Sand } Unfortunately, not all sand marketed for rodents/small animals is safe for hamsters. Make sure you check before buying! Things to look out for to avoid buying unsafe sand: "Bathing Dust" - The fine particles from the dust can cause respiratory issues for hamsters. It is used for chinchillas and degus, so if the packaging clearly states "chinchilla dust", stay away! Calcium - Calcium sand is designed to clump up and harden, which can cause internal blockages if ingested. Artifical Colour/Dye - Dyes contain chemicals that are harmful for hamsters. They can cause skin and respiratory irritation and can be toxic if ingested. 3kg sÅN@Y NUMBER

text: UNSAFE Team Top Tip! If you are unsure about the materials or fibres in your chosen bedding, Bedding } contact the manufacturer to ensure it is safe for your hamster. Alternatively, swap to a bedding you know is safe! 1 1 1 1 SHAVINGS LEMON wooo SHAVINGS PILLOW WAD. Woodshavings vi ngs md e h ft Cozy Snowflake woodshavings natural pet bedding o ill] Sawdust / Woodshavings Most sawdust/woodshaving bedding is made from pine and cedar wood. There are harmful chemicals found in these types of wood which can be toxic and irritant for hamsters. The fine particles in sawdust is also known to cause respiratory problems and infections. Fluffy Bedding This includes any materials similar to cotton wool, kapok fibre or bamboo fluff. Though they look cosy, they can cause serious harm. The material can enter the lungs causing respiratory issues and/or be ingested and create fatal blockages. Scented Bedding Hamsters have very sensistive noses and use scent to navigate their surroundings. Scented bedding will cause stress, irritate their nose and even cause respiratory infections. NUMBER
